plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 41: Atomic Structure
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.

elements: vertical z-axis with arrowhead at top, labeled z
horizontal axis crossing the z-axis at the origin (unlabeled)
origin point at the axis intersection, set at left of frame
seven olive-green arrows of identical length fanning from the origin into the right half-plane at angles θm = arccos(m/√(l(l+1))) for m = -3…3 with l = 3
bold arrow labeled L with vector arrow on the topmost (steepest) green arrow
dashed circular arc of radius |L| = ħ√(l(l+1)) passing through all arrow tips, spanning from +z to -z on the right side
dashed horizontal projection lines from each arrow tip back to the z-axis

four thin angle arcs of increasing radius sweeping from the +z axis to the four upper arrows, labeled θ0 (smallest radius, opening to the horizontal arrow), θ1, θ2, θ3 (largest radius, closing on the steepest arrow)

interactions.label: Step through m
interactions.teaches: Each allowed vector has a z-component of exactly mħ landing on a matching tick, while the vector length |L| never changes — only the z-projection is quantized

interactions.label: Orientations
interactions.teaches: A faint continuous fan of every possible orientation contrasts with the seven allowed vectors, showing quantum mechanics permits only selected polar angles, not any direction

interactions.label: Quantum number l
interactions.teaches: Raising l gives 2l+1 allowed projections mħ from −lħ to +lħ and lengthens every vector to ħ√(l(l+1)), linking the angular-momentum magnitude to the count of allowed Lz values

demo_steps.title: Seven allowed orientations
demo_steps.narration: For l = 3 there are 2l+1 = 7 arrows, all the same length ħ√12 ≈ 3.46ħ, tips on the dashed arc. Their z-components step in equal ħ units from −3ħ to +3ħ.

demo_steps.title: Quantized projection
demo_steps.narration: Step through m. One arrow highlights at a time and its dashed projection line lands exactly on the mħ tick — the z-component is quantized even though the vector itself never lies along z (max Lz = 3ħ < |L|).

demo_steps.title: Not just any angle
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the continuous fan: every orientation would be classically allowed, but only the seven discrete directions survive — space quantization.

demo_steps.title: Smaller l
demo_steps.narration: Set l = 1: only 3 arrows remain (m = −1, 0, 1), the arc shrinks to radius ħ√2, and the angular gaps widen — fewer, coarser allowed orientations.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Pure 2D diagram in the x–z plane, viewed front-on. World units: 1 unit = ħ on the z-axis. For l: vector length R = √(l(l+1)) units; arrow for magnetic quantum number m points at polar angle θm = arccos(m/√(l(l+1))) measured from +z, so tip = (R·sinθm, m). For l=3: R≈3.46, angles from +z: 30.0°, 54.7°, 73.2°, 90°, 106.8°, 125.3°, 150°. Origin at left-of-center; z-axis vertical spanning −(l+0.8) to +(l+0.8), horizontal axis short, extending ~1 unit left and ~R+0.5 right of origin. Arrows olive/yellow-green (#8aa61e-ish, matching source), thick shafts with filled heads; topmost arrow carries label 'L' with a small vector arrow above it, placed just right of its tip. Dashed circular arc radius R from +z pole to −z pole on the right half, grey. Dashed horizontal lines from each tip leftward to the z-axis, grey. Tick labels 3ħ…−3ħ placed left of the z-axis at each integer. Angle arcs θ0…θ3: thin black arcs centered at origin from the +z axis to arrows m=0,1,2,3 respectively, radii increasing (~0.7, 1.1, 1.5, 1.9 units for l=3) so they nest without overlap; labels sit just outside each arc near its midpoint. Highlighted arrow in the m-step state: brighten/thicken it and color its projection line and tick label. Continuous view: ~40 faint grey-green arrows evenly spaced in angle behind the discrete set.
interactionPlan.notes: All arrows, the dashed arc, projection lines, tick labels, and θ arcs must be regenerated reactively when l changes (arrow count = 2l+1, labels renumbered θ0…θl). Keep z-axis extent fixed per l so the arc visibly grows with l. Render arrows as flat 2D shapes (cylinder+cone or extruded polygons) in the z=0 plane with an orthographic camera. In Continuous mode show both the faint fan and the bold discrete arrows.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button / state for allowed m values: the learner steps through m = -3 to 3, one green L vector highlights at a time and its dashed projection lands on the matching hbar tick, showing that the z component is quantized while the vector length stays fixed.
- Toggle between discrete and continuous angles: the learner switches from the seven allowed vectors to a faint continuous fan, making clear that the diagram permits only selected polar angles rather than any orientation.
- Slider for quantum number l: the learner changes l, the number of allowed projection states and the common vector length update together, revealing how angular-momentum magnitude and allowed Lz values are linked.

authoredContext:
The quantization of the polar angle for the l=3 state is shown in the figure. The orbital angular momentum vector lies somewhere on the surface of a cone with an opening angle θ relative to the z-axis (unless m=0, in which case θ=90° and the vector points are perpendicular to the z-axis).

The quantization of orbital angular momentum. Each vector lies on the surface of a cone with axis along the z-axis.

Seven vector, all of the same length L, are drawn at 7 different angles to the z axis. The z components of the vectors are indicated both by horizontal lines from the tip of the vector to the z axis and by labels on the z axis. For four of the vectors, the angle between the z axis and the vector is also labeled. The z component values are 3 h bar at angle theta sub three, 2 h bar at angle theta sub two, h bar at angle theta sub one, zero at angle theta sub zero, minus h bar, minus 2 h bar, and minus 3 h bar.

A detailed study of angular momentum reveals that we cannot know all three components simultaneously. In the previous section, the z-component of orbital angular momentum has definite values that depend on the quantum number m. This implies that we cannot know both x- and y-components of angular momentum, Lx and Ly, with certainty. As a result, the precise direction of the orbital angular momentum vector is unknown.
